content.comment_body: I have several sensors operating at different voltages, such as 12V and 5V. How can I connect the common (M) of the PLC to the negative terminals of the sensors' power supply without causing damage to the PLC or creating ground loops? Also, what is the purpose of earthing in this setup?

You can connect the common (M) of different power supplies together. However, if the common of one or more power supplies is connected to protective earth, then the protective isolation of the [product_name] may no longer be maintained.

"is the protective isolation of the [product_name] may no longer be maintained." Could you clarify what you mean by this? Is it safe to connect the grounds of different voltage supplies together, or does this risk creating ground loops?
I also have a question. Is it necessary to connect common (M) to Field Earth (FE)?

Hello, If you are using discrete inputs, refer to the relevant table: the input will register a state 1 starting from either 8.5V or 12V depending on the [product_name] model you have. Therefore, if your sensor operates at 5V, it may not trigger a state 1.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are discussing how to properly and safely connect sensors with various power supply voltages (e.g., 5V and 12V) to a PLC. The conversation centers on grounding techniques, the risks of ground loops, and how protective isolation might be affected when merging power supply commons and earthing. There is also a focus on ensuring compatibility with discrete input voltage requirements on [product_name] modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for practical solutions that enable them to connect multiple sensors with differing voltage levels to a PLC safely, without risking PLC damage or ground loop formation. They seek clear guidance on grounding, earthing practices, and input voltage compatibility.
